notes.summary: Primary-source audit: the published class body proves ambient volume only; Xia’s body retains I-equivalence and leaves zero-volume dimension conjectural; Cao and CHPW require distinctions and hypotheses absent from a general P-sensitive theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: The four supplied source hashes were checked. DRWNXZ requires a smooth complete flag and proves ambient volume equals class volume/n!. Xia section 5.6 explicitly states Conjecture 5.29 rather than proving its numerical-dimension equality. His multiplier-ideal construction is I-invariant, and its volume formula concerns the I-envelope. Cao’s product uses absolutely continuous parts of quasi-equisingular approximants. CHPW’s numerical theorem requires a flag containing a positive volume subvariety on a smooth projective variety. None supplies unchanged original P15.3.
notes.text:
The inspected versions are DRWNXZ arXiv:2309.07584v3, Xia arXiv:2112.04290v2, Cao arXiv:1210.5692v1, and CHPW arXiv:1508.03922v5. Their supplied PDF and extract hashes matched. The extract line counts, computed using split('\n'), are respectively 2034, 2700, 1931, and 1425.

DRWNXZ Definition 3.2 and the pseudoeffective definition, lines 561–691, construct bodies from successive Lelong valuations along a globally smooth connected complete flag. Theorem 7.6 and Corollary 7.7, lines 1389–1415, prove vol_Rn(Delta)=vol(alpha)/n!. The nonbig proof compares with perturbations and concludes zero ambient volume. It does not prove a lower-dimensional numerical theorem or retain prescribed potential data. Definition 5.1 and Example 5.3, lines 852–894, do impose bounded singularity order for analytic Kähler reference currents.

Xia’s section spaces use I(k phi), so I-equivalent inputs give identical bodies. Proposition 5.8 and section 5.6 retain this invariance. Section 5.6, lines 1623–1637, defines the perturbative intersection and literally states Conjecture 5.29: dim Delta(theta,phi)=nd(theta,phi). Its following sentences refer to Cao’s definition and express an expectation about a proof. This is not a proved equality. Xia’s definitions, lines 371–429, distinguish bounded type, ordinary P-envelope, C-envelope, and I-envelope. At zero actual mass Proposition 2.10 does not identify C with P. Theorem 2.19 computes section volume from the mass of P[phi]_I, not unconditionally from the actual mass of phi. Class volume, ideal-model volume, and actual potential mass must therefore be kept separate.

Cao Definitions 2–4, lines 162–289, use quasi-equisingular analytic approximation and absolutely continuous parts to define a cohomological product. Definition 3 concerns general positive currents; Definition 4 is stated for line bundles with metrics. Identifying this product with an actual nonpluripolar product requires an additional argument.

CHPW Theorem B/Corollary 3.22 requires a smooth projective variety, a pseudoeffective real divisor, and a flag containing a positive volume subvariety. Its lower-dimensional mass is augmented restricted volume along that subvariety. Remark 3.24 explicitly allows strict dimension inequality for other flags. These results cannot simply be applied to arbitrary transcendental classes or arbitrary flags.

Literal statements and relevant proof bodies, exact versions and LF locations, hashes, and application checks are preserved in source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Complete byte-identical extracts are also preserved. Rerun: python3 prepare_sources.py. These are source findings, not a proof that original P15.3 is impossible.

notes.summary: Restricted genuine P-sensitive construction: rational divisorial data with smooth residual give a perturbation-independent translated body. A nonprojective transcendental product example has dimension 2, recovers coefficient a, and has unnormalized mass kappa²−a².
notes.detailedSummary: For T=beta+[D], with beta smooth semipositive and D=aF a rational smooth divisor, the positive-perturbation partial current-valuation bodies equal nu(D)+Delta([beta]+epsilon[Omega]). Their intersection is independent of the stated positive perturbations. A transverse maximum argument proves P_theta[phi]=phi+O(1). In a specified blowup of a transcendental Kähler surface times a curve, an explicit product-body identity proves dimension 2 and twice the area equals kappa²−a². Actual and Cao cohomological products agree in this analytic domain. Arbitrary nonanalytic P-types and general numerical equality remain outside the result.
notes.text:
Use dd^c=i partial-barpartial/(2 pi). Fix a compact Kähler manifold with a globally smooth complete flag, a smooth prime divisor F, rational a>0, and D=aF. Suppose T=theta+dd^c phi=beta+[D], where phi is the logarithmic divisor potential and beta is smooth closed semipositive. Assume class volume zero. Define B as the intersection of the genuine DRWNXZ partial bodies for T+epsilon Omega, with admissible analytic currents more singular than phi up to a bounded constant.

At every epsilon>0, the reference is Kähler with gentle analytic singularities. Adding [D] to a residual analytic Kähler current gives an admissible current and translates its valuation by nu(D). Conversely, admissibility forces multiplicity at least a on F. Divisor subtraction leaves a positive analytic residual; subtracting from G−delta Omega proves that residual is Kähler. The published analytic-current realization places its valuation in the residual class body. Hence Delta(alpha+epsilon[Omega];T+epsilon Omega)=nu(D)+Delta([beta]+epsilon[Omega]), and B=nu(D)+Delta([beta]). It is nonempty, compact, and convex.

Adding a smooth positive form preserves valuations. Pointwise comparisons c Omega<Omega'<C Omega sandwich the residual bodies after rescaling epsilon, proving independence of the Kähler perturbation form. Smooth positive perturbations tending to zero are similarly sandwiched by the fixed-form nested bodies. Compactness proves Hausdorff convergence to their intersection. No nonpositive-path independence is claimed.

The retained P-data are proved directly. For a normalized competitor v<=phi+C, subtract [D] and write its residual potential w=v−phi. Away from F, v<=0 bounds w uniformly. In coordinates F={z_1=0}, add a local smooth potential of beta. On fixed transverse circles this psh function has a uniform upper bound independent of C. The subharmonic maximum principle extends it across the transverse discs. A finite cover gives v<=phi+K uniformly. This logarithmic bound survives envelope regularization; phi−sup phi supplies the reverse bound. Thus P_theta[phi]=phi+O(1). Boundedly equivalent inputs have identical envelope competitor families and identical body constraints.

For numerical content, take a compact Kähler surface S with Kähler class kappa outside the real span of divisor classes. Such input exists on a generic complex two-torus with no nonzero integral (1,1)-classes. Blow up p, obtaining pi:S_hat→S and exceptional E. A cutoff logarithmic potential u_a=a chi log(|z_1|²+|z_2|²), for sufficiently small rational a>0, has positive curvature. On the blowup its current is beta_a+a[E], where beta_a is smooth Kähler in kappa_a=pi*kappa−a[E]. In blowup coordinates z_1=w,z_2=wt, subtracting the divisor leaves pi*kappa_form+a dd^c log(1+|t|²), positive normally and tangentially; the cutoff annulus is controlled by choosing a small.

On X=S_hat×C use the flag X⊃S_hat×{c_0}⊃E×{c_0}⊃{(q,c_0)}. The original class on S×C is pulled back from kappa, and the prescribed original potential is the pullback of u_a. The specified modification supplies a complete smooth flag. The psh pullback bijection in this nonbig class is proved by descending off the exceptional image, extending bounded-above psh potentials across it, and using uniqueness of canonical psh representatives. This order isomorphism also preserves ordinary envelope competitor families. No independence of unrelated modifications or flags is asserted.

Let beta be the pullback of beta_a. For Omega_0=p_S_hat*eta+p_C*sigma with integral_C sigma=1, the exact product identity is Delta_Y([beta]+epsilon[Omega_0])=[0,epsilon]×Delta_(E,q)(kappa_a+epsilon[eta]). For the upper inclusion, subtract the first valuation t and restrict to a generic curve fiber; positivity gives epsilon−t>=0. The remaining flag restriction has surface class kappa_a+epsilon[eta]. For the lower inclusion, pull back a surface analytic Kähler current R and add the curve current (epsilon−t)sigma+t[c_0], for rational 0<=t<epsilon. Its valuation is (t,nu(R)); density and closure give the identity.

Intersecting and using continuity from above for the big surface class gives B={(0,a+x,y):(x,y)∈Delta_(E,q)(kappa_a)}. The surface body has nonempty interior, so B has intrinsic dimension 2 and affine carrier {x_1=0}. Its standard coordinate area satisfies 2! Area(B)=integral beta_a²=kappa²−a²>0. This follows from the published surface volume identity, pi*kappa.E=0, and E²=−1. Its minimum second coordinate is a, since the surface body contains the origin. Thus distinct a give distinct bodies in the same original class, genuinely retaining the prescribed analytic P-type.

Class volume is zero independently: a hypothetical Kähler current in the pulled-back class, paired with its smooth semipositive representative squared, contradicts the zero cube. Actual nonpluripolar products of beta+[D] are beta^k by locality off D and absence of pluripolar mass. The constant analytic approximation computes Cao’s current products as [beta^k]. The largest nonzero degree is 2. For boundedly equivalent representatives the bounded Bedford–Taylor telescoping identity proves the same cohomological products. This proves equality in this domain, not generally. The unnormalized mass is the surface integral; a transverse reference form of degree m would multiply its threefold pairing by m. No zero mass is normalized.

The complete proof is in P15.3-argument.md and standalone P15.3-paper.tex. This is an unverified restricted theorem, not complete coverage of original P15.3.

notes.summary: Exact obstruction: a zero-volume P-envelope with poles on dense fibers admits no more-singular nontrivial potential analytic near any flag center, even after positive Kähler perturbation. This defeats the direct analytic-domination recipe, not original P15.3 itself.
notes.detailedSummary: On P¹×C, a summable sequence of positive rational logarithmic poles at dense base points defines a legitimate zero-mass potential in a zero-volume class. Its ordinary P-envelope retains every fiber pole by the uniform single-divisor envelope bound from n2. Any more-singular potential must have a dense minus-infinity locus, incompatible with analytic singularities on any open neighborhood. The impossibility is for that competitor rule and does not exclude another geometric realization.
notes.text:
Take M=P¹×C and theta=p_1*omega_FS, with integral omega_FS=1. Its class is pseudoeffective and nonbig: pairing a hypothetical Kähler current with theta contradicts theta²=0 and integral Omega wedge theta>0. Thus class volume is zero.

Choose distinct dense points p_j on P¹ and a_j=2^(−j−2), j>=1, whose sum is A=1/4. Let g_j<=0 be the logarithm of squared chordal distance to p_j. Then dd^c g_j=[p_j]−omega_FS, and its L1 norm is independent of p_j by unitary invariance. The decreasing series u=sum a_j p_1*g_j has summable L1 norms, so it defines a nontrivial theta-psh potential. Distributionally, theta+dd^c u=(1−A)theta+sum a_j[F_j], where F_j={p_j}×C. Its actual top nonpluripolar mass is separately zero because every bounded truncation is pulled back from the curve.

Put psi=P_theta[u] with zero obstacle. Since u<=a_j p_1*g_j, envelope competitor inclusion and the single-divisor bound proved in n2 give psi<=P_theta[a_j p_1*g_j]<=a_j p_1*g_j+K_j. Thus psi is minus infinity on every F_j. The competitor u ensures the envelope is nontrivial.

Suppose a nontrivial quasi-psh v satisfies v<=psi+C and has analytic singularities on any open neighborhood. It is minus infinity on the dense union of the fibers. Locally an analytic potential has minus-infinity locus equal to a closed holomorphic zero set, or the empty set. Containing a dense set forces that zero set to be the whole neighborhood, making every generator identically zero and v identically minus infinity there. This contradicts local integrability of a nontrivial quasi-psh potential.

The argument is independent of the background form. Therefore no such analytic competitor exists in PSH(M,theta+epsilon Omega), for any Kähler Omega and epsilon>0, even if analyticity is required only near a flag center. Consequently the direct recipe of valuing analytic currents more singular than a fixed P-envelope and intersecting perturbative bodies cannot handle arbitrary prescribed P-data. Another genuine valuation or geometric construction remains possible in principle; no impossibility theorem for unchanged original P15.3 is claimed.

The complete obstruction proof appears in Section 4 of P15.3-argument.md and in P15.3-paper.tex.
